clue.text: Grouse or duck seized by male or female bird of prey

indicators.note: something seized by a group is held inside it, so the duck goes within the run that follows

parts.note: an owl is a nocturnal bird of prey
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A game bird or a duck is caught by a raptor of either sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'or' is only a link. 'seized by' tells you the duck goes inside, and a duck is cricket's score of nothing, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorfowl is another name for the red grouse of upland heather moors.

clue.text: Highly amusing person coming in second best

parts.note: the cream of anything is its best part

explanation.surface: A very funny comedian finishes runner-up rather than winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a scream is an informal idiom for a hilariously funny person.

clue.text: Leader of climbers always upset when fool falls in this?

definitions.text: Leader of climbers always upset when fool falls in this?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from climbers
'in' puts one piece inside the other
in a down clue an upset word is turned over, so its letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A lead climber is forever dismayed when an idiot tumbles into a crack in the glacier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EVER into REVE; C, REVE and ASS join. The whole clue also describes the deep glacier crack a careless climber might fall into.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep fissure in a glacier that a careless mountaineer could fall down.

clue.text: More nastily derogatory about rackets being raised

indicators.note: in a down clue something raised is lifted upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A spiteful remark about noisy disturbances escalating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being raised' turns RE DINS upwards, giving the letters in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Snide means sneeringly disparaging, so its comparative form means more nastily derogatory.

clue.text: Rousing stuff, timeless symphony

indicators.note: timeless says the T, the abbreviation for time, is removed from the word before

explanation.surface: A stirring, enduring symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rousing stuff' looks like praise for the music but is arousing material, EROTICA; 'timeless' drops its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Third Symphony is known by its Italian title, the heroic one.

clue.text: Team adding numbers before and after this

definitions.text: Team adding numbers before and after this

parts.words: Team adding numbers before and after this
parts.note: a football or cricket side, with arithmetic on the neighbouring whole numbers: this figure sits between ten and twelve

explanation.walkthrough: A cricket or football side has this many players; the rest of the clue plays on the numbers either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket team has this many players, so a side is called by the number.

clue.text: Pressed on in awfully dire case

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the case formed by the other
awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of dire are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pushed on in a terrible situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges the four letters of 'dire' to make IRED. Read 'in ... case' together as the container signal: 'case' is part of it, not a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed clothes are ironed, smoothed flat with a hot iron.

clue.text: A lot of people caught up in party machine

indicators.note: in places the turned word within the party
in a down clue being taken up means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: many means a lot of people

explanation.surface: Lots of people get swept up in a political party's machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught up' turns MANY into YNAM, which goes 'in' DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a machine that generates electricity from rotation.

clue.text: Parts of solutions put across for areas with social problems?

definitions.meaning: a hint to the puzzle's theme: city names sit in the middles of answers entered across

explanation.walkthrough: Brendan's theme: cities are hidden inside across answers, such as LIMA in CLIMACTERIC, so they are cities within.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner-city districts are the deprived central parts of large towns, often linked with social problems.

clue.text: Red Cross hero that's automatically put in control?

definitions.meaning: St ..., the saint whose red cross is England's flag
an aircraft's automatic pilot is nicknamed with this man's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Cross' is not the charity but the red cross of England's patron saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint George is England's patron saint, and pilots call the autopilot by the same name.

clue.text: Woman and man in partnership for people of Western state

indicators.note: in sets the couple inside the partnership

parts.note: North-South is a bridge partnership, abbreviated NS

explanation.surface: A woman and a man entering a partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players form two pairs, North-South and East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is a western US state; Nevadans are its inhabitants.

clue.text: That woman with old idol, a priestess

explanation.surface: A woman worships an ancient idol as its priestess.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'idol' and 'a priestess' define: Hero was the priestess of Aphrodite loved by Leander.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone admired as a champion, and in Greek myth Hero was Aphrodite's priestess.

clue.text: Realms most disrupted in turbulent situations

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kingdoms thrown into chaos in stormy times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges REALMS MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool, figuratively any chaotic, turbulent state of affairs.

clue.text: Priest holding one mass, something done in critical time

indicators.note: holding means the priest contains the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an act is something done, a deed

explanation.surface: A priest conducting a single Mass at a crucial moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something done' means a deed. 'mass' is the physics abbreviation, not the church service the priest suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A climacteric is a critical period or turning point, especially in a person's life.

clue.text: Traveller with story about popular female shopkeeper

indicators.note: about means going round, so the traveller encloses the next piece

parts.note: the Miller is one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims who tells a tale

explanation.surface: A traveller tells a tale about a well-liked woman who keeps a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The traveller with a story is a Canterbury pilgrim: Chaucer's pilgrims each tell a tale on the road to Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner makes and sells women's hats, traditionally a woman running a hat shop.

clue.text: Seal unit off to avoid shocking accidents

definitions.text: Seal unit off to avoid shocking accidents

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Close up a device to prevent electric shocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SEAL UNIT; the whole clue describes the job of covering wiring with non-conducting material.
explanation.definitionFit: To insulate is to cover with non-conducting material so electric current cannot cause shocks.

clue.text: Make use of library as author

definitions.meaning: George ..., nineteenth-century English writer of travel books such as Lavengro

explanation.definitionFit: Library users take books out on loan, and George Borrow was an English travel writer.

clue.text: On edge that's hard?

definitions.meaning: something not easy is hard, read as un- plus easy

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word into a prefix meaning 'not' and a word for simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uneasy is anxious, on edge; read as not easy it also means hard.

clue.text: Assumes position tardily in America

parts.note: a post is a position or job

indicators.note: in puts the lateness inside the country

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: Takes up a job late in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position' is a job here, not where something stands, and 'Assumes' means takes as given, not takes up.
explanation.definitionFit: To postulate is to assume something as true as a basis for reasoning.

clue.text: Numbers split up in US city

indicators.note: split up means broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Figures broken down for an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split up' rearranges COUNTS, a word for numbers, not the clue's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucson is a city in southern Arizona.

clue.text: Communist council among, also, Vietnamese

indicators.note: among says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A communist body that includes Vietnamese members too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' points to the run inside ALSO VIETNAMESE.
explanation.definitionFit: A soviet was an elected workers' council in the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Dispatch starts from southern England, finishes in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: starts are the first letters of the words that follow
finishes are the last letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Posting something from the south of England to Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts from' takes S and E; 'finishes in' takes N and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch something is to send it off.

clue.text: Regularly perform exploit in force

indicators.note: in places the exploit inside the forcing

parts.note: to prise is to force open
an act is a deed or exploit

explanation.surface: Routinely carry out a feat by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' is a verb, as in forcing a lid open, and the setter uses the British spelling with -ise.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise is to perform an activity regularly to get better at it.

clue.text: Put together very badly as houses

parts.note: ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Something assembled very poorly, like a shoddy housing development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put together' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Villas are large detached houses, often in the country or abroad.

clue.text: Like most drivers, stiff and awkward

definitions.meaning: golf drivers, the woods, traditionally had heads of wood
lacking natural ease, as in a stilted acting performance

explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' are golf clubs, not motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf drivers were traditionally made with wooden heads; a wooden performance is stiff and clumsy.

clue.text: Guard's second appearance

parts.note: an entry is an appearance, as of an actor onto the stage

explanation.surface: A security guard turns up for the second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep guard.
